title: HEX notation
learningObjectives: Explain hex notation and apply it correctly in a small CSS example.

understand.concept: CSS hexadecimal colours describe RGB channel values using # followed by three or six hexadecimal digits. The six-digit form is #RRGGBB; the three-digit shorthand expands each digit, so #abc becomes #aabbcc. An optional alpha channel can be written with four or eight digits.
understand.whyItMatters: Each pair represents red, green, and blue intensity from 00 to ff. Hexadecimal is base 16, so digits include 0–9 and a–f. The eight-digit form is #RRGGBBAA; the final pair controls alpha.
understand.analogy: A colour code is like three labelled intensity controls written compactly. It is not a colour name and it does not describe a paint brand or guarantee perceptual brightness.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy helps build intuition, but the browser follows the CSS specifications and computed-style rules rather than human intentions.

explain.narrative: The swatch has a blue background, white text, and a darker blue border. Change #2f80ed to #e76f51 and observe the result.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to learn the effect of a CSS value?
options: Change one value and inspect the rendered result
Add unrelated declarations until it looks right
Assume every browser calculates styles identically in every context
questions.answer: Change one value and inspect the rendered result
questions.explanation: Controlled experiments make it easier to connect a CSS declaration with its visible effect.
